## operationsFromContract() function

Check a generated contract against its manifest and build its registered operations.

**Signature:**

```typescript
declare function operationsFromContract(
  contract: AppContract<unknown>,
  manifest: AppManifest
): RegisteredOperation[]
```

**Returns:**

[RegisteredOperation](./runtime.registeredoperation.md)<!-- -->\[\]

One registered operation per contract descriptor, using the contract's descriptors.

## Exceptions

[OperationRegistrationError](./runtime.operationregistrationerror.md) on any disagreement, when the app's route segment is reserved ([RESERVED_APP_ROUTE_SEGMENTS](./runtime.reserved_app_route_segments.md)<!-- -->), when a command that must select one item declares no identifier parameter, or when a resource's identifier declares no targeting and is not the class's dictionary id.

## Remarks

Every descriptor must name an operation the manifest exposes, under the key it is filed by, with exactly the manifest-derived permission and target. Checking the target as well as the permission matters: a descriptor that kept a read permission but pointed at a destructive command would otherwise run that command under the read grant. A descriptor also takes the paging inputs exactly when the manifest says its list pages (`listOperationPages`<!-- -->), so a contract generated before an identifier's uniqueness claim changed is refused rather than paging a list that cannot be anchored reliably.

The manifest itself must pass the checks registration from the manifest alone applies: every command that must select one item declares a required identifier parameter (`unselectableItemCommands` in `@macts/core`<!-- -->), and every resource whose primary identifier declares no targeting is identified by the class's dictionary id (`untargetedIdentifiers`<!-- -->). A manifest those checks refuse registers nothing through a contract either, whichever operations the contract covers.

A contract may cover a subset of the manifest's operations. Its resource table must agree with the manifest too: every resource it lists is one the manifest declares, with the identifier type of the manifest's primary identifier property. Each registered operation carries the table's value plans (`resourcePlanTable`<!-- -->).

Exported so a contract can be checked against its manifest without constructing a runtime, for example when verifying generated packages.
